text: The marshmallow test measured more than willpower.
The famous version: a Stanford preschool, and follow-ups with thirty-five to eighty-nine kids.
So researchers retested it with nine hundred eighteen kids.
Age four. Wait seven minutes, get more.
In the main group, waiting predicted scores at fifteen. But half as strongly.
Then they accounted for family background, the home, and early thinking skills.
The link shrank by two thirds.
Kids who waited often had richer homes, and stronger early skills.
So the marshmallow test measured more than willpower.
